notes.summary: In One Word Substitution a phrase or definition is given and you choose the single word that means the same. Words come in families (people, fear/phobias, killing, government, study of), so learning them by group is fastest.

concepts.title: Learn by families
concepts.body:
• -cide (killing): homicide, regicide, fratricide, infanticide
  • -logy (study of): ornithology (birds), entomology (insects), seismology (earthquakes)
  • -cracy (rule by): autocracy, democracy, plutocracy (rule by the rich)
  • -phobia (fear): acrophobia (heights), claustrophobia (closed spaces)

concepts.title: Break the definition
concepts.body: Find the key idea in the definition (who? what? which action?) and match it with the root. One who cannot be corrected → key idea 'cannot be corrected' → incorrigible.

varieties.name: Words for people
varieties.how: Identify the role or habit described, then recall the word.

varieties.name: Root families (-cide, -logy, -cracy, -phobia)
varieties.how: Match the subject (bird, king, fear) with the right root.

varieties.name: General definitions
varieties.how: Focus on the key idea; eliminate words from a different family.

tips: Revise one family (e.g. all -cide words) at a time.
Options often come from the same family; know the exact root to choose correctly.

questions.q:
Select the word that can substitute the given group of words.
The study of birds
questions.solution: ornith = bird, -logy = study. Ornithology. Entomology = insects; Anthropology = humans.

questions.q:
Select the word that can substitute the given group of words.
A person who loves mankind and works for its welfare
questions.solution: phil = love, anthropos = man. Philanthropist. A misanthrope hates mankind; a philatelist collects stamps.

questions.q:
Select the word that can substitute the given group of words.
That which cannot be read
questions.solution: Illegible = cannot be read (of handwriting). Ineligible = not qualified; inaudible = cannot be heard.

questions.q:
Select the word that can substitute the given group of words.
Government by the wealthy
questions.solution: plutos = wealth, -cracy = rule. Plutocracy. Aristocracy = rule by nobles; autocracy = rule by one person.

questions.q:
Select the word that can substitute the given group of words.
A person who is unable to be corrected or reformed
questions.solution: Incorrigible = cannot be corrected. Invincible = cannot be defeated; indefatigable = never tired; inexorable = cannot be stopped or persuaded.

questions.q:
Select the word that can substitute the given group of words.
A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
questions.solution: Agenda = list of items to be discussed at a meeting. Inventory = list of goods in stock; manifesto = public declaration of policy.
